name: Tuy Hoa
provinceNote: Resolution 202/2025/QH15, clause 15, prints Phú Yên and Đắk Lắk as the new Đắk Lắk province: 18.096,40 km² and 3.346.853 people. It does not name a capital. Decision 759/QĐ-TTg, dated 14 April 2025, places the administrative center at present-day Buôn Ma Thuột and prints 18.096,4 km² and 2.831.300 people. The area pair is the same sketch printed two ways. The populations are not the same. The national tourism bureau still prints 5.060,6 km² and 893,4 thousand people (2015), with the capital at Tuy Hòa. None of those figures is chosen.
dotReason: The night on the Độc Lập beach is the reason to stop.
summary: Basalt columns at Ganh Da Dia meet the sea north of Tuy Hoa, and Mui Dien to the south is the easternmost point of the mainland. Swim the white sand on Doc Lap under the casuarinas, climb Nhan Tower above the Da Rang, and eat chive noodle soup and ocean tuna. One day on the beach, with the columns as the trip north.
timeNeeded: One day on the sand. The columns at Ganh Da Dia are the trip north.
fee: The handbook gives about 10.000 đồng a person for Mũi Điện. Other sights bill separately. Check on arrival.
getThere: Tuy Hòa airport, 5 km north or about 10 km, or Ga Tuy Hòa.
seoTitle: Tuy Hoa travel guide — Ganh Da Dia, Mui Dien, the city beach
seoDescription: Basalt columns at Ganh Da Dia, the easternmost cape at Mui Dien, and the white sand on Độc Lập. Quy Nhon is about 90 km up the coast.
intro: Ghềnh Đá Đĩa, which locals call gành Đá Dĩa, is the basalt where it meets the sea north of town, and the city beach on Độc Lập is the swim you wake to: white sand tens of metres wide, casuarina behind it, and beachfront buildings along the road. One account gives a front longer than 10 km. Another gives about 10 km, sea on one side and the town lights on the other. Both lengths stay. Swim here and eat seafood on the shore. Stay when this front is the trip. Go to Quy Nhon, about 90 km up the coast, when the next city is the trip, or on to Nha Trang when the island boats are.

Give a morning to Tháp Nhạn, the brick tower on Núi Nhạn, on the north bank of the Đà Rằng. The bureau dates it to the late 11th or early 12th century: four storeys, nearly 23,5 m, each side of the foot 10 m, a door to the east, and a lotus-bud stone. The heritage page gives a different measurement: a base 12,2 m by 12,2 m, a body about 9 m by 9 m, and the base and body together 12,4 m, in a yard 38 m by 38 m. Do not quote one height. The hill is about 60 m on the heritage page and the handbook, and 64 m on the English tourism page. Both stay. The bureau describes a small shrine and no statue. The heritage page says the worship is Poh Nagar, the east door had collapsed, and the present door is 2,4 m high. Ranked a national architectural relic on 16 November 1988. Ranked a special national relic by Quyết định 1820/QĐ-TTg on 24 December 2018. Saturday at 19:30 the English page puts a show in the yard, named “Phu Yen – the attractive and friendly destination.”

The stone plates and the cape are day trips from this bed. Ghềnh Đá Đĩa, which locals call gành Đá Dĩa, is the basalt where it meets the sea. The tourism bureau places it at xã An Ninh Đông, huyện Tuy An, Phú Yên, more than 50 m wide and about 200 m long, and ranks it a national landscape in 1998. A news account gives 50 m wide and more than 2.000 m long, and a national ranking in 2005. A later account places the same rocks at xã Tuy An Đông, tỉnh Đắk Lắk, old name An Ninh Đông, with a main area of about 2.700 m², a tilted north point and a mostly vertical south point, a 1997 national ranking, and a 2020 special-national ranking. All three size lines stay. All three ranking years stay. The routes stay too: about 30 km on QL1A to Chí Thạnh then about 12 km east; about 35 km from the center; about 40 km north via Tuy An Bắc and nhà thờ Mằng Lăng.

Bãi Môn–Mũi Đại Lãnh, also Mũi Điện, is the cape to the south. The tourism bureau gives a crescent of about 400 m. The old district page gives more than 400 m. The light is a pair of descriptions. The bureau: about 26 m, about 108 wooden steps, 27 hải lý, built in 1890, repaired from August 1996, working in 1997. The district page: 25,6 m, diameter 4,5 m, 107 steps, main light 28 hải lý at 110 m, a second light 18 hải lý at 92 m, built in the early 1920s, rebuilt from 1995, working in 1997. The district page calls it the easternmost point of the mainland and the first sunrise. The handbook gives a visit fee of about 10.000 đồng a person. The river under the hill is the Đà Rằng, which the bureau also calls sông Ba. Cầu Đà Rằng has 21 spans and is called the longest bridge in central Vietnam on that page.
gettingAround: Cảng hàng không Tuy Hòa is the airport. The 2024 AIP, VVTH, prints 5 km north of the city center, operating hours 2300–1400, not converted, and the telephone +84 257 3851950. The handbook prints about 10 km from the center. Both distances stay. The operator page prints the office at Đại lộ Hùng Vương, phường Phú Yên, tỉnh Đắk Lắk, phone 02573851950. The handbook names Vietnam Airlines, Bamboo Airways, and VietJet Air from Hà Nội and TP Hồ Chí Minh, and a round-trip range of 1,5–5 triệu đồng. That range is not an airport tax. Flight minutes were not printed. Check on arrival.

Ga Tuy Hòa is on the unified rail table. Southbound the row is km 1198. Northbound the row is km 528. A street number was not on that table. Check on arrival. Southbound cells are all ngày +1. Diêu Trì to Tuy Hòa: SE7 04:12 then 06:34, SE5 06:02 then 08:12, SE9 12:29 then 14:19, SE3 16:54 then 19:08, SE1 18:50 then 20:38. Tuy Hòa to Nha Trang: SE7 06:34 then 08:47, SE5 08:12 then 10:25, SE9 14:19 then 17:03, SE3 19:08 then 21:12, SE1 20:38 then 22:42. Northbound, Nha Trang to Tuy Hòa: SE8 14:03 then 16:10, SE6 16:13 then 18:32, SE4 02:47 (ngày +1) then 04:55 (ngày +1), SE2 03:51 (ngày +1) then 05:57 (ngày +1). SE10 has no Tuy Hòa cell. Tuy Hòa to Diêu Trì: SE8 16:10 then 18:07, SE6 18:32 then 20:39, SE4 04:55 (ngày +1) then 06:51 (ngày +1), SE2 05:57 (ngày +1) then 08:02 (ngày +1). A second railways page prints different Tuy Hòa cells: southbound SE3 19.00, SE1 19.35, SE5 09.11, SE7 06.59; northbound SE4 04.57, SE2 05.55, SE6 18.24, SE8 15.51. Both sets stay. Do not pick one. Neither table prints a fare. The handbook prints 400.000–1.000.000 đồng by seat and origin.

QL1A is the coast road. Quy Nhon is about 90 km on the handbook. The minutes were not printed. From Hà Nội the bureau prints 1.177 km and the handbook prints about 1.200 km. From TP Hồ Chí Minh the bureau prints 561 km and the handbook prints about 500 km. A city-to-city kilometre for Nha Trang was not printed. About 100 km on the cape page is from Nha Trang to mid Đèo Cả, not to this city. A sleeper from Bến xe Miền Đông at 17h or 18h arrives early the next morning. The return fare on that page is 540.000 đồng a person. The Tuy Hòa bus-station name was not printed. A taxi fare was not printed. Kilometres and minutes to Buôn Ma Thuột were not printed. Check on arrival. On site, the swim is the east beach along Độc Lập. The tower is about 1,5 km from cửa Đà Diễn. Minutes from the beach to the hill were not printed. North to the plates: about 30 km on QL1A to Chí Thạnh then about 12 km east, or about 35 km from the center, or about 40 km north via Tuy An Bắc and nhà thờ Mằng Lăng. South to the cape: about 35 km southeast, and also 23 km on QL1A to mid Đèo Cả plus about 12 km. The old district page prints 35 km south, and 15 km to the old Đông Hòa center then 20 km, then a path of about 500 m.

stayAreas.name: Doc Lap
stayAreas.summary: Sleep on the beachfront along Độc Lập when the sand is the point. The handbook says the city still has few high-end resorts. A brand is not a pick.

stayAreas.name: The river and April First square
stayAreas.summary: Sleep in the center by the Đà Rằng and Quảng trường 1/4 when the evening is the square. A street number for the square was not printed. No hotel brand is a pick.

eat: Bánh canh hẹ is the local bowl: soft strands, sea-fish cake, and a lot of chives. One account says the strand can be bột lọc or bột gạo. The handbook says it is sold all day at chợ Tuy Hòa, on the Trần Hưng Đạo side of the market, and at the Ngô Quyền and Trần Hưng Đạo corner.

Cá ngừ đại dương, also called cá bò gù, is the fish along Lê Duẩn and bờ kè Bạch Đằng. Thin slices go in mustard greens. The eye is steamed, with spices or with thuốc bắc. In 2017 the tourism page says mắt cá ngừ đại dương hầm thuốc bắc was named in a Vietnam-records food list. Sò huyết from Đầm Ô Loan is pink with yellow roe, grilled on charcoal until the liquor runs, then a little salt, pepper, and lime. The handbook also names nướng tái, xào me, hấp, gỏi, and rang muối ớt. Cua Huỳnh Đế is red or yellow on the shell while still alive, with a tuft of short yellow hair, and walks forward because the claws sit at the front. The lagoon is 1.300 ha on the tourism page and 1.570 ha, about 1,3 m deep, on the handbook. Both areas stay. It is 25 km north.
interestsBody: The night is the walk on Độc Lập, sea on one side and the town lights on the other. The morning on that sand is for exercise. Quảng trường 1/4 is the center evening.
Tháp Nhạn is the brick tower on the hill, about 60 m on two pages and 64 m on the English page. Saturday at 19:30 is the show in the yard.

To carry home, the handbook names frozen tuna and tuna eye, dried squid, bò một nắng, bánh tráng, mắm cá cơm, and shell crafts. Rượu Quán Đế comes from Xuân Lộc and Xuân Bình in Sông Cầu. The stone plates and the cape light are the day trips. Their sizes and the two descriptions of the light are in the introduction.

interestGroups.title: Dining and F&B
interestGroups.summary: Bánh canh hẹ at the market, the tuna eye, and sò huyết from Đầm Ô Loan.
body: Du lịch Phú Yên’s 6 October 2024 cẩm nang sells bánh canh hẹ all day at chợ Tuy Hòa. The tuna eye is the plate on Lê Duẩn and bờ kè Bạch Đằng. Sò huyết from Đầm Ô Loan is grilled until the liquor runs.

cards.title: Dining and F&B
cards.summary: Bánh canh hẹ, the tuna eye, and sò huyết from Đầm Ô Loan.

interestGroups.title: Ganh Da Dia
interestGroups.summary: Basalt columns where they meet the sea, north of town.

cards.title: Ganh Da Dia
cards.summary: Walk the black columns where they meet the sea. Locals say gành Đá Dĩa.

interestGroups.title: The city sand
interestGroups.summary: The swim and the night walk on Độc Lập, for a stay that is this beach.
body: The sand is east of town along Độc Lập. It is white, tens of metres wide, with casuarina and the beachfront buildings. One account gives a front longer than 10 km. Another gives about 10 km. Morning is for exercise. Evening is the walk, sea on one side and the town lights on the other. Seafood is eaten on the shore.
The swim is this city sand on Độc Lập. Nghinh Phong, at the Nguyễn Hữu Thọ and Độc Lập corner, is the square the handbook puts a light show on at night. It is a different yard from Tháp Nhạn.

cards.title: Tuy Hoa beach
cards.summary: The city sand on Độc Lập. Longer than 10 km on one account, about 10 km on the night account.

interestGroups.title: The Cham hill
interestGroups.summary: A morning at the brick tower above the river, before the Saturday show.
body: Tháp Nhạn stands on Núi Nhạn, on the north bank. The bureau prints nearly 23,5 m. The heritage page prints a base and body of 12,4 m. Those are different measurements. The hill is about 60 m on the heritage page and the handbook, and 64 m on the English page. The bureau describes no statue, and a small shrine. The heritage page says the worship is Poh Nagar.
It was ranked a national architectural relic on 16 November 1988 and a special national relic on 24 December 2018.

cards.title: Nhan Tower
cards.summary: The brick tower on the hill. Nearly 23,5 m on the bureau page, and 12,4 m for the base and body on the heritage page.

interestGroups.title: The river
interestGroups.summary: The Đà Rằng under the hill, and the long bridge of 21 spans.
body: The bureau also calls this river sông Ba. Cầu Đà Rằng has 21 spans and is called the longest bridge in central Vietnam on that page. The tower looks down on the water.
The center evening is Quảng trường 1/4.

cards.title: Da Rang river
cards.summary: The river and the long bridge. The bureau gives 21 spans.

interestGroups.title: Saturday at the tower
interestGroups.summary: One evening a week in the tower yard, for people already in town.
body: The English tourism page schedules a show every Saturday at 19:30, named “Phu Yen – the attractive and friendly destination.” It does not run that line on other nights.

cards.title: Saturday at the tower
cards.summary: 19:30 on Saturday in the tower yard.

interestGroups.title: Shopping
interestGroups.summary: Chợ Tuy Hòa for bánh canh hẹ, and tuna and bò một nắng to carry home.

cards.title: Shopping
cards.summary: Chợ Tuy Hòa on the Trần Hưng Đạo side for bánh canh hẹ. Frozen tuna, dried squid, and bò một nắng are the things to carry home.

faqs.q: Where is the Tuy Hoa beach?
faqs.a: Bãi biển Tuy Hòa is the sand east of this city along Độc Lập. One account gives a front longer than 10 km. The night account gives about 10 km. Both lengths stay.

faqs.q: How far is Tuy Hoa airport from the city?
faqs.a: The 2024 AIP gives 5 km north of the city center. The provincial handbook gives about 10 km. Both stay. The AIP hours are 2300–1400 and are not converted here.

faqs.q: Which train time to Tuy Hoa should I use?
faqs.a: The unified table and a second railways page do not match. On the unified table, southbound SE7 reaches Tuy Hòa at 06:34 the next day. The second page prints SE7 at 06.59. Northbound, the unified table’s SE8 is 16:10 and the second page prints 15.51. Do not pick one. Neither table prints a fare. The handbook prints 400.000–1.000.000 đồng by seat and origin. The full cells are in Getting there.

season.label: Easier Jan–Aug
season.note: The tourism bureau’s climate line is an annual average of 26,5ºC, a high of 39ºC, and a low of 15,5ºC, hot, humid, and rainy. The handbook gives rain from September to December and the easier months January to August. Both stay. The AIP’s 27,6°C is the aerodrome figure, not this climate line. Lunar rites move on the solar calendar.
